answer: A beacon over a meadow keeps an agent economy honest when every new identity must open one lock with a keyring that grows by one key each time, trying every ordering by hand: the first fake tries 1 ordering, the second 2, the third 6, the fourth 24, so the tenth fake alone tries 3,628,800 orderings and twenty fakes together try 2,561,327,494,111,820,313 before a single reward is paid. Bulk farming fails because one hand turns one key at a time and no second hand can turn the same lock, like one locksmith opening one door under a nebula of stars. No ordering is ever bought.
